analysis.title: Stocks, Bonds, & Oil All Up Amid 'Red October' Rout Across Europe
key_insights: Oct 1-2 session was chaotic: Iran-war correlations broke down, oil, stocks, bonds, the dollar, gold and crypto all rose while the euro fell sharply.

Brent crude rebounded above $100. Desk chatter attributes the move to rebuilt war premium, not a new supply outage: Rubio expelling Iran's UN delegation, a US push for France and Germany to release diesel stocks or face a possible US export ban, the Abqaiq strike, and Trump saying Iran developments are coming 'very soon'.

Physical oil markets show tightness: record premiums for immediate supply at the biggest US storage hub, and Dated Brent at a wide premium to futures. Capital Economics calls the market structurally tight after about six months of inventory drawdowns.

The Pentagon is sending a third carrier strike group and more Marine ships to the Middle East (9,000-10,000 more troops) arriving by end of November, while Trump says stepping up bombing of Iran is possible after the midterms.

Treasury yields and rate-hike expectations fell despite higher oil, a hot ISM Prices Paid reading and hawkish Fed speakers. The short end led the drop after Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said judging whether more hikes are needed 'may take more time'.

A global bond selloff hit Europe on Thursday, with French OATs and Italian BTPs widening and French CDS jumping. US Treasuries caught a safe-haven bid and 10-year yields pulled back from a 24-year high. RBC's Izaac Brook said the move was about overseas yields, not US data.

Fed speakers were mostly hawkish: Kashkari, Collins, Schmid and Barkin said inflation is the focus given a stable labor market. Kashkari noted the 2-year yield (about 4.88%) is far above the roughly 4% 2-year yield implied by the SEP.
The Treasury buyback accepted the full $6B for the first time, against more than $46B offered, but the curve still steepened.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky sees yields near tactical upside exhaustion after the 30-year moved from 5.25% to 5.69% in 7 sessions, with bond Daily Sentiment at 10%. Falling yields could reverse the QQQ vs IWM ratio and push QQQ and Mag7 lower.

Equities were choppy. Micron gave upbeat current-quarter guidance on AI demand but warned rising compensation would weigh on margins. NDX and RTY led, the Dow was flat and the SPX had small gains. Mag7 closed unchanged and lagged the S&P 493.

ISM manufacturing came in slightly below expectations, but Prices Paid was in the top 20% of readings in the series' 75-year history. Bloomberg's Simon White shows higher manufacturing prices lead S&P forward P/Es lower by 6-12 months.
New lows exceeded new highs for the 13th straight day. Goldman's desk said it was about 3% better to buy, with activity at 4 out of 10, ahead of Friday's payrolls.

The dollar tested the top of its 18-month range, with EUR at its weakest against the dollar since May 2025. Gold held green and bitcoin rose back to about $85k despite the first ETF outflow in a while.

Krinsky calls October the 'Bear Killer', but the three prior October lows followed drawdowns of about 48%, 22% and 27%. The SPX is roughly flat since June and near all-time highs, with 9 of 11 sectors down more than 2% over the last month, while put/call ratios are near yearly lows and VIX Daily Sentiment is 19%, so he sees a high risk of a high-correlation index volatility event in October.

sector_views.rationale: Long-only funds were skewed slightly to sellers of financials, communication services, materials and industrials and buyers of info tech, health care and macro products. Hedge funds were better buyers in macro products, info tech, financials and consumer discretionary, with supply in materials and health care.
